    "hypothesis": "Predicted that nonface objects containing salient Gestalt information (connectedness, closure, and continuity) would elicit holistic processing similar to that observed for faces, even in the absence of expertise.",
    "design": "mixed, with task (face vs. line pattern) as a between-subjects factor and alignment (aligned vs. misaligned) and congruency (congruent vs. incongruent) as within-subjects factors.",
    "manipulation_or_predictor": "The presence of Gestalt information in line patterns (connectedness, closure, and continuity) and the alignment of top and bottom parts of the stimuli.",
    "outcome_measure": "Response sensitivity (d') in a composite-task paradigm, measuring the congruency effect (difference in sensitivity between congruent and incongruent trials) across aligned and misaligned conditions.",
    "population_and_setting": "22 participants recruited at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics.",
    "sample_size_total": 22,
    "recruitment_and_incentive": "Not stated.",
    "analysis_plan": "A 2 (alignment) x 2 (congruency) x 2 (task) repeated measures ANOVA to test for the presence of holistic processing, specifically looking for a Congruency x Alignment interaction.",
    "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
    "other_methods_notes": "Participants performed two composite tasks (faces and line patterns). The composite task involved same/different judgments of the top halves of stimuli while ignoring the bottom halves. The study used a complete design of the composite task."
